rar5: Detect 32 bit size_t overflows

If a parsed value does not fit into 32 bit size_t, treat it as error
instead of truncating.

While auditing the size handling here, correct the link target length
check in parse_file_extra_redir(): target_size is a byte count passed
to read_ahead() and memcpy(), but it was compared against
MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS - 1, a character count.  Compare it against
MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES - 1 instead, which matches the byte size of
target_utf8_buf.

Reported-by: krishna28238-arch <krishna28238-arch@users.noreply.github.com>
Signed-off-by: Maintainer D <maintainer-d@example.invalid>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

rar5: Adjust read_var/read_var_sized return values

USE ARCHIVE_OK, ARCHIVE_EOF, and ARCHIVE_FATAL for improved error
handling. Integer overflows must not be considered "end of file".

Handle different error message on 32 bit systems in tests.

Also shrink parse_file_extra_redir()'s on-stack target buffer to
MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS to reduce the function's stack footprint.

Signed-off-by: Maintainer D <maintainer-d@example.invalid>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: The defect lives in the memcpy() at the end of parse_file_extra_redir() in the RAR5 reader: it copies an attacker-controlled link target of target_size bytes out of the archive into the on-stack target_utf8_buf and then NUL-terminates at [target_size]. Neither edited commit touches the memcpy; each edits one side of the two-sided size contract that keeps it safe. The first edited commit (7346bd0) relaxes the admission check from target_size > MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS - 1 (2047) to target_size > MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES - 1 (8191), framing it as a byte-vs-character unit correction - in its own tree the buffer is still MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES (8192) bytes, so the wider check is exactly right and verifiably safe. The second edited commit (a2d4178) shrinks target_utf8_buf from MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES to MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS (2048) to cut the frame's stack footprint - in its own tree the check still admits at most 2047 bytes, so the smaller buffer is exactly right and verifiably safe. Only the composition admits up to 8191 bytes into a 2048-byte buffer: a RAR5 FILE header carrying an EX_REDIR extra field with a target longer than 2047 bytes then drives a stack-buffer-overflow write reachable from archive_read_next_header() on the public API. The bug is not reachable from either edit alone: with only the first, the copy still lands in an 8192-byte buffer; with only the second, the 2047-byte cap still bounds the copy below the 2048-byte buffer. A fix confined to a single edited diff cannot clear the defect without discarding that commit's (individually correct) maintenance: the first commit's check is the proper byte-unit comparison given the buffer its author sees, and the second commit's buffer matches the cap its author sees in the pre-edit series. The correct repair is inherently cross-commit - the admitted length must be tied to the buffer that actually receives the copy (e.g. bound target_size by sizeof(target_utf8_buf) - 1, or restore consistency across both hunks) - which requires reasoning about the two hunks, and the contract between them, together.
